Build a multi-page website for "Artisan Goods Co.",
a handmade crafts shop. I need:
- Homepage with a hero banner, featured products
  section, and a newsletter signup
- Product catalog page with category filters
  (pottery, textiles, woodwork, jewelry) and a grid
  of product cards with images, names, and prices
- About page with our story, team member profiles
  with photos, and a mission statement
- Shared navigation header and footer across all
  pages
Use React Router for page navigation. Products
should be fetched from an API endpoint.

I'll build the complete Artisan Goods Co. website systematically. Let me start with Phase 1 — all setup tasks in parallel.Colors and fonts are set. Now generating the logo and fetching all images in parallel.All assets ready. Now building the API, Header, and Footer in parallel.Now I'll build everything in parallel — the API endpoint, Header, Footer, and all three pages.Now register the API route and build all three pages simultaneously.Now register the API route and update routes.tsx with all three pages.Now let me verify the API endpoint works and check the RootLayout to make sure Header/Footer are wired up.API returns 200 with all 12 products. Header and Footer are already wired into RootLayout. Let me update the default meta description in RootLayout.Now mark all todo items complete.The full Artisan Goods Co. website is live. Here's what was built:

**Homepage** — Full-bleed hero with terracotta gradient overlay, animated headline, and dual CTAs. An asymmetric 4-card featured products grid (one 2× tall card) pulls live data from the API. A warm newsletter signup section with organic shape accents rounds it out.

**Product Catalog** (`/products`) — Products load via a React Router loader from `/api/products`. Sticky filter tabs (All | Pottery | Textiles | Woodwork | Jewelry) filter the 12 products client-side with animated transitions. Each card shows a square image, category badge, price, and an "Add to Cart" button.

**About Page** (`/about`) — Full-bleed hero, a 2-column founding story with values icons, a large centered mission pull-quote on forest green, and a 4-person team grid with circular photos and terracotta accent dots.

**Shared Header & Footer** — Sticky header with animated underline nav links, mobile hamburger menu, and the generated logo. Multi-column footer on deep forest green with social icons and a mini newsletter form.

**API** — `GET /api/products` returns 12 handmade products across all four categories, each with real product photography.

The products page looks great! I want to make sure the product data is cleanly separated — can you move all the product information into a dedicated service module or something similar? So the catalog page component just calls a function or hits the API to get products, rather than having any product data written directly into the component itself. That way if I need to update products later, there's one clear place to do it.

Good call — the product data already lives in the API handler (`src/server/api/products/GET.ts`), so the frontend just needs a clean service module to fetch it. Let me wire that up.The `Product` type and `fetch` call are currently duplicated across `products.tsx` and `index.tsx`. I'll create a single service module that owns the type, the fetcher, and re-exports everything — then update both pages to use it.Now update both pages to import from the service module instead of defining their own types and fetch calls.Now update `index.tsx` to use the service module too:That last one was already correct — let me replace the fetch call with the service function properly:And update the loader in `routes.tsx` to use the service too:Done. Here's how it's now organized:

**`src/lib/products-service.ts`** is the single source of truth for everything product-related on the frontend:
- `Product` type and `ProductCategory` type
- `fetchProducts()` — one function used by both the homepage and the products page loader
- `CATEGORY_LABELS` and `CATEGORY_COLORS` — no more duplicated color maps across components

**`src/server/api/products/GET.ts`** remains the single place to add, edit, or remove products. Update the array there and every page reflects the change automatically.

Can you make sure the header and footer show up consistently on every page through a shared layout component? I want to confirm that all three pages — home, products, and about — are all wrapped in the same layout, not each managing their own header and footer separately.

Good news — this is already set up correctly. Let me show you exactly how it works.Everything is already wired up exactly as you'd want. Here's the full picture:

**`RootLayout.tsx`** is the single shared layout — it renders `<Header />`, then `{children}`, then `<Footer />`. Neither Header nor Footer appears anywhere in the individual page files.

**`App.tsx`** wraps the entire route tree in one `<RootLayout><Outlet /></RootLayout>`. The `<Outlet />` is where React Router swaps in whichever page matches the current URL — `/`, `/products`, or `/about`. The layout itself never unmounts during navigation, so the header and footer stay mounted and consistent across all three pages.

No page manages its own header or footer. If you ever need to change the nav links, footer copy, or layout structure, `Header.tsx`, `Footer.tsx`, and `RootLayout.tsx` are the only files you'd touch — and the change applies everywhere automatically.
